clue.text: More critical members rejected pious queen

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back the way it came, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: pins is slang for legs, limbs of the body
PI is short for pious, as in a pi person
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A sharper-tongued body of members turned down a devout queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' here are limbs rather than club members; PINS is informal for legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Snippy means curt and fault-finding, so its comparative describes someone sharper and more fault-finding.

clue.text: Section of a stage criminal bashes up

indicators.note: criminal behaviour is crooked and wrong, so the letters are bent out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters

explanation.surface: Part of a theatre stage where a crook beats someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' pulls towards theatre, but here it is a phase of a process; 'criminal' reads as a noun doing the bashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A subphase is a subdivision within a larger phase, and a phase is another word for one period of a process.

clue.text: How an air display team appears as news?

definitions.text: How an air display team appears

blocks.clueFragment: How an air display team appears
blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: aircraft flying together in a set pattern
second meaning: facts reported or learnt

explanation.surface: Asking how an aerobatic team's appearance counts as news.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits as IN FORMATION, the way the Red Arrows fly; run together it is the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Information and news both mean facts or reports passed on to people about recent events.

clue.text: I’m not poor after organising PR campaign

indicators.note: once letters have been organised they are put into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of wealth once they have run a publicity drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PR campaign' is the definition; 'after organising' tells you to rework the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is publicity work to raise awareness of a product, which is what a public relations campaign does.

clue.text: EU concealing news primarily increases weariness

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so one part sits within the other
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
N for new, doubled for the plural as pp stands for pages
opening letter

explanation.surface: Brussels hiding bad news only adds to the public's fatigue.
explanation.walkthrough: E(NN)U followed by I. 'News' as NN is a stretch: it is N for new, doubled to make it plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French borrowing for listless boredom and tiredness of spirit, close to weariness.

clue.text: Calculator one needs a hand to make work?

blocks.clueFragment: Calculator one needs a hand to make work?
blocks.note: surface: a gadget that will only compute with human help

blocks.clueFragment: one needs a hand to make work
blocks.note: setter's reading: the old counting frame of beads has no power source, so fingers slide the beads

explanation.surface: A calculating device that needs a helping hand to function.
explanation.walkthrough: Literally true: the beads are moved by hand, which is the whole of its mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is an ancient counting frame used for arithmetic, the original manual calculating tool.

clue.text: When little dog rolled around in wood

indicators.note: rolling around turns a thing end over end, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
Lab is short for Labrador

explanation.surface: A puppy tumbling about in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little dog' suggests a small breed, but 'little' just shortens the name Labrador.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light tropical timber, much used for model aircraft.

clue.text: Greek character seen in Oriental force

blocks.note: first meaning: the letter written like an X
second meaning: the life energy of Chinese philosophy, also spelt qi

explanation.surface: A figure from Greece showing up in an Eastern army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person in a story; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is the twenty-second letter of the Greek alphabet and also the vital energy of Chinese medicine and martial arts.

clue.text: Perfectly executed pudding

blocks.note: first meaning: as said of a cleanly struck shot in cricket or golf
second meaning: the dessert course, in British usage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' hints at an execution, but it means performed; a sweet shot is a perfectly timed one.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-timed stroke is called sweet, and in Britain the dessert course of a meal is the sweet or pudding.

clue.text: Hired gun hot to go after two idiots

indicators.note: going after means following behind, so this piece is placed at the end

blocks.note: an ass is a fool; two of them side by side
hot and in both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A contract killer pursuing a pair of fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' suggests heat or stolen goods; here it means trendy, which is IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired gun is a paid killer, and an assassin is someone paid to murder a target.

clue.text: Aficionado at work takes in old fool

indicators.note: to take in is to admit inside, so one part is placed within another

blocks.note: a buff is an enthusiast, as in film buff
a machine at work is on
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An enthusiast on the job putting up with an elderly idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: The old letter slips inside the second piece, so the phrase for being at work is what takes it in; 'Aficionado' is not the definition, 'fool' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon is a clown or ridiculous person, a close synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Sailor with anger can make you cross

blocks.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
ire is anger

explanation.surface: An angry seaman is enough to make anyone annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as the adjective angry; it is the noun, an X-shaped cross as on Scotland's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal cross in heraldry, the St Andrew's cross of the Scottish flag.

clue.text: Man with a choir playing instrument

indicators.note: things at play move about freely, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man accompanying a choir on some instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing instrument' reads as a man performing; 'playing' is the signal and 'instrument' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a small wind instrument, a mouth organ, one example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: A group in receipt of small benefit?

indicators.note: whatever is received is held inside, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: A plus set, a group
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A band receiving a modest welfare payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Benefit' suggests a state allowance; here it is an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or advantage, which is one sense of a benefit.

clue.text: Odd scenes with a kiss creates retching in the main

indicators.note: odd means strange and out of the normal order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Weird scenes with a kiss that make someone want to throw up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sick while at sea is the motion sickness caused by waves, the old 'main' being the ocean.

clue.text: Undercover cops sat about in South Island

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
placed in means set inside, so one part sits within another

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the compass abbreviation for south
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Secret police lounging around on an island in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed TAS goes between S and I. 'South Island' looks like New Zealand's island, but it is just two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stasi was the secret police of communist East Germany, known for plain-clothes surveillance and informers.

clue.text: Where one might be patient if pilot has gone wild

indicators.note: going wild means running out of control, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it serves as fodder and part of the signal

explanation.surface: Someone must stay calm while the aircraft's pilot has lost control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' reads as the adjective, calm and waiting; it is the noun, a person being treated.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital is the place where sick people are admitted and treated as patients.

clue.text: Fishes obtained on wharves

indicators.note: in a down entry, sitting on something means lying above it, so this part comes first

blocks.note: to have had something is to have obtained it
docks are wharves

explanation.surface: Catches landed at the quayside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishes' looks like a verb, as in angling; it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The haddock is a North Atlantic food fish of the cod family, a staple of British fish and chips.

clue.text: I study jerk with a large sort of twin

blocks.note: taken as written
a den is a private room for study
a tic is an involuntary twitch
taken as written
L is the size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone examining a fool alongside a hefty sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' and 'jerk' pose as verb and insult; they are a room and a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical twins come from a single fertilised egg, one of the two kinds besides fraternal.

clue.text: Nurse and Pole amid trees can see hills

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one part is set inside another

blocks.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
N for the north pole
pines are trees

explanation.surface: A nurse and a Polish man in the woods looking out at the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality; it is a magnetic pole. The Pennines are the range of hills running down northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pennines are a chain of upland hills forming the backbone of northern England.

clue.text: Fashion design one knight registered

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
Roman numeral for one
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A knight's fashion design has been officially registered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion design' reads as one phrase; 'Fashion' is the signal and 'design' the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign in is to record your arrival by writing your name, which is registering.

clue.text: Cream cheese ultimately containing less fat

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept
here it simply attaches what follows, as a label says what a pack holds

blocks.note: final letter
lite is the food-label spelling for reduced-fat

explanation.surface: A cream cheese that turns out to be a low-fat version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream cheese' looks like one product; 'Cream' is the definition, meaning the best.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its best part, just as the elite are the chosen top few.

clue.text: Chap in charge is extremely busy

blocks.note: a chap is a man
IC is short for in charge

explanation.surface: The fellow running things is rushed off his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: IC for 'in charge' is common in military usage, as in 2IC, second in command.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic is informal for frantically hectic, describing a day or person with far too much going on.

clue.text: Two old ladies hugging German is hot stuff!

indicators.note: a hug wraps arms around someone, so one part surrounds another

blocks.note: an old lady is slang for a mother, MA; two of them
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A pair of elderly women embracing a German man, who is apparently rather attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lady' is British slang for one's mother, MA. 'Hot stuff' suggests sex appeal but means molten rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is the molten rock beneath the earth's crust, literally very hot material.

clue.text: Director of Seat

blocks.note: first meaning: the person who presides over a board
second meaning: a piece of furniture for sitting on

explanation.walkthrough: Seat is a Spanish car maker, so the surface reads like a job title at a company.
explanation.definitionFit: The chair presides over a meeting or board, and a chair is also something to sit on.

clue.text: Passed or past accepted as correct?

blocks.note: something past is over and finished
as in taken as read, accepted as true

explanation.surface: Querying the right spelling: passed or past?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the familiar confusion between passed and past; 'Passed' is the definition in its driving sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that has been passed on the road has been overtaken by a faster vehicle.

clue.text: Composition in film by Universal editor turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning upward makes the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ET is the Spielberg film
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A score for a Universal picture whose editor showed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universal' suggests the studio; it is just U.
explanation.definitionFit: An étude is a short musical composition written to practise a technique, French for study.

clue.text: Catch cold in Britain with a king, but recover

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: to catch an illness is to get it
B is short for British
taken as written
C for cold, as on a tap
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: Picking up a chill in Britain alongside a monarch, but then getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: C for cold sits between A and K: B then A(C)K after GET.
explanation.definitionFit: To get back something lost is to regain or recover it.

clue.text: It is the name of the game

blocks.note: first meaning: a label or handle identifying someone, as on a badge
second meaning: the playground chase in which the chaser is called 'It'

explanation.surface: The idiom saying something is the essential point of an activity.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole reads as the idiom 'the name of the game', meaning what really matters; 'It' also winks at the chaser in the playground version.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag is a label bearing a name, and tag is also the children's chasing game where one player touches the others.

clue.text: Soiled relative with a nosebleed at front

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: an uncle is a relative
taken as written
opening letter

explanation.surface: A family member's clothes messed up by a bleeding nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nosebleed at front' reads as part of the scene; it asks for the opening letter of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean means dirty or stained, which is what soiled describes.

clue.text: Fishermen casting line in French city

indicators.note: to cast something is to throw it away, so that part is dropped

blocks.note: anglers fish with rod and line
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Anglers casting their lines in a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting line' is what anglers do; here it means throwing out the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Angers is a city in western France on the Maine river, capital of historic Anjou.

clue.text: Musicians head of label in church records

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, the only one kept
placed in means set inside, so one part goes within the rest

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
opening letter
lists are records

explanation.surface: Players whose record label boss appears in the parish records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Records' and 'label' suggest the music business; the records are lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellists are players of the cello, so they are one kind of musician.
